affectedPublicSurfaces: Every authenticated `/v1/*` request: the unit-of-work seam in `database/database.py` now applies `SET LOCAL app.current_shop_id` (shop-scoped majority) and `SET LOCAL app.current_user_id` (user-scoped tables) inside each tenant-scoped transaction, with the values read from the already-resolved active shop and user. No route contract, status code, or body changes — the settings are read by nobody until #1328's policies land, and that invisibility is itself the release property to verify.

Every Celery task: worker units of work derive their tenant from the run's shop (never from a request, never from any default or reference shop) and fail closed with a named error when the run cannot be resolved. Beat tasks that are genuinely fleet-wide (reconcile, backfill top-up, impact reader, reaper, credential refresh) run under a single named, logged `system_scope()` escape.

The fail-closed boundary itself: a tenant-scoped unit of work opened with neither a tenant context nor `system_scope()` raises a named Python error BEFORE any SQL is emitted. This is new refusal behaviour on the runtime path — wrong in the too-strict direction it refuses every request, which is why the candidate journey proves normal traffic end to end.

Mixed-version note: the seam lives in shared backend code loaded by both `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` on the single-VPS lane (ADR-057). The change is behaviourally invisible while the deployed system connects as `postgres` and no policy reads the GUCs, so old and new processes coexist; a worker restarted onto the new release simply starts setting GUCs nothing consumes yet.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: pytest with PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree's backend/src; all pool-behaviour claims (SET LOCAL cleared on checkout return, two sequential tenants on one pooled connection each seeing only their own value) run against a real pooled Postgres 16 engine on a scratch database — never an in-memory session, which cannot make a pool claim. Post-deploy: the candidate is exercised with ordinary authenticated traffic against the sandbox/test seller only; no production credential is used for any write and no public traffic is routed to a candidate task set (the single-VPS lane has none).
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: workersDisabledOnCandidate is FALSE deliberately: the Celery half of the seam (task tenant derived from the run's shop; beat tasks under system_scope()) can only be proven with a worker running — a beat task under system_scope() must be observed completing end to end, not stubbed. The journey's entire point is behavioural invisibility: with the app still connecting as postgres and zero policies reading the GUCs, every request and task must complete exactly as before, with the only observable difference being the transaction-scoped settings and the system_scope() log records.

journeys.name: seam-applied-and-behaviourally-invisible
assertions: pre-merge: a unit of work opened without a tenant context and without system_scope() raises the named error before any SQL is emitted — asserted by observing that no statement reached the database (statement capture on the engine), not merely that an exception occurred

pre-merge: on a real pooled Postgres engine, after a tenant-scoped transaction commits and the connection returns to the pool, a fresh checkout observes app.current_shop_id and app.current_user_id unset — SET LOCAL, never SET
pre-merge: two sequential units of work for different tenants on the SAME pooled connection each observe only their own value — the cross-tenant leak this decision exists to prevent

pre-merge: system_scope() emits a log record naming the caller, its transactions are exempt from the fail-closed assertion, and a test enumerates the system_scope() call sites so the exemption list cannot grow silently

pre-merge: a Celery task resolves its tenant from the run's shop and fails closed with the named error when the run cannot be resolved — no fallback to any default or reference shop, asserted by the absence of any such query
pre-merge: the existing suite passes unchanged as postgres, and core/security/dependencies.py shows a zero-line diff

post-deploy: on the candidate, an authenticated read, an approve, an SSE stream and one beat task each complete normally — behaviourally identical responses while the process still connects as postgres and no policy reads the GUCs
post-deploy: the system_scope() log records for the beat task name the calling task, and no request is refused by the fail-closed assertion during the journey window

htmlRoutes: No HTML route, page, bundle, or static asset changes — the diff is backend Python (database/database.py, a request/task tenant context module, workers) plus tests.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration. The seam sets transaction-scoped GUCs that no policy reads yet (#1328 adds the readers) — setting an unread GUC is schema-neutral and version-neutral, so the stable release and the candidate coexist against the same database. If implementation concludes it needs any schema change, this plan must be revised BEFORE merge; nothing here may write a policy — that is #1328's slice and would be inert-or-dangerous out of order.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Without the seam, behaviour is exactly today's: the GUCs are never set and the ten existing policies remain dead. No new exposure — the wave's isolation chain simply stays blocked at its first backend link.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. The seam is additive (a GUC nothing consumes), so rollback is code-only with no data or schema residue. THE ONE ORDERING HAZARD: a revert must not be able to leave the fail-closed assertion active without the setter — that combination refuses every request. The setter and the fail-closed assertion ship in the same module and the same commit, and a test asserts the pairing (the assertion is unreachable without the seam being importable), so a whole-release revert removes both together; partial cherry-picks of this slice are forbidden.

acceptanceCommands: PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests/unit -k 'tenant_context or system_scope or unit_of_work' -q
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/juli_exec_1327 PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests/integration -k 'tenant_context or set_local or pooled' -q
ruff check backend tests && ruff format --check backend tests
doNotInfer: core/security/dependencies.py is W6 #1313's file and must not appear in this PR's diff. The seam reads the ALREADY-RESOLVED active shop and user at the unit of work — it does not touch auth resolution.

SET LOCAL, never SET: session-scoped settings leak one tenant's context into the next pool checkout. Every pool-behaviour claim runs on a real pooled Postgres engine — an in-memory or mocked session proves nothing about the pool.

No policy is written in this slice. Policies are #1328's; writing them against a setter that just landed inverts the chain ADR-085 fixed. The GUCs being read by nobody in this slice is deliberate and is what makes the setter provable in isolation.

Celery tenant resolution derives from the run's shop and fails closed when the run cannot be resolved — never a fallback to any default shop, reference shop, or DEMO_REFERENCE_SHOP_ID. A bug must never render as another tenant's context.
system_scope() is a named, logged decision in the code: the beat tasks it exempts are enumerated by a test, and adding a call site without updating the enumeration fails.

The DATABASE_URL cutover to juli_app is gate #1339 observation 1 — an owner act. This slice changes nothing about which role the deployed system connects as, and writes stay sandbox-bound: nothing targets Fujiwa Vietnam Store (2b1da87b).
